 Pinned Trump takes midterm campaign to Kansas as GOP defends Senate seat
 ​ 
 President Donald Trump 
 is scheduled to campaign in Kansas on Monday for Republican Sen. Roger Marshall as the GOP works to defend its Senate majority.
 The rally in Wichita is part of Trump’s expanding midterm campaign push for Republican candidates across the country.Marshall is facing a competitive reelection race against Democrat Adam Hamilton, a Methodist minister, in a state that has traditionally been considered safely Republican.
 Trump has increasingly placed himself at the center of the midterm elections, urging voters to preserve Republican control of Congress and warning that Democrats would seek to reverse his second-term agenda.
 President Donald Trump departs a campaign rally at Dalton Municipal Airport, Friday, Oct. 16, 2026, in Dalton Ga. (AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein)
 Posted by Bradford Betz Share Massachusetts GOP ticket rocked by alleged drunken crash as candidate abruptly halts campaign
 Shawn Oliver holds a sign supporting Republican gubernatorial nominee Mike Minogue. (Shawn Oliver for Lt. Governor Facebook)
 A late-night crash has thrown a Massachusetts Republican’s statewide campaign into turmoil just weeks before voters head to the polls.
Shawn Oliver, 42, the Republican nominee for lieutenant governor and a New Bedford city councilor, suspended his campaign on Sunday. The move came after Oliver was arrested following a rollover crash that involved five parked vehicles, police confirmed to Fox News Digital.
 Officers responded around 11:40 p.m. Saturday to 448 Dartmouth St., where a vehicle had overturned after striking multiple parked vehicles, the New Bedford Police Department said. Two of the five parked vehicles sustained extensive damage.

 Posted by Stepheny Price Share Booker rival who ‘shoots from the hip’ hopes viral debate moment can break GOP’s Senate drought
 Sen. Cory Booker, D-N.J., attends the Phoenix Awards Dinner during the Congressional Black Caucus Foundation (CBCF) at the Walter E. Washington Convention Center on Sept. 19, 2026 in Washington, D.C. (Monica Morgan/Getty Images)
 A New Jersey attorney and former municipal official who made waves during his debate with Sen. Cory Booker 
, D-N.J., said his unscripted style may be the secret sauce to making history and ending a Republican Senate drought in New Jersey that stretches back more than half a century.
 Justin Murphy, a Navy veteran and former deputy mayor of Tabernacle in the state’s Pine Barrens, stunned his incumbent Democratic opponent when, in response to a question about the Iran war strategy, he bluntly said President Donald Trump should forcefully "finish it."
 "I don’t have a speechwriter. There’s no teleprompter — I shoot from the hip because I want people to see a very sincere, genuine and authentic Justin Murphy," Murphy told Fox News Digital.
 This is an excerpt from an article by Fox News Digital's Charles Creitz and Kiera McDonald — click here to read more 
 Posted by Charles Creitz Share Early voting commences in multiple states as midterms heat up this Monday
 Voting booths are seen at an early voting site at the Orange County, Florida Supervisor of Elections Office on the last business day before early voting begins for the Nov. 3, 2026 midterm elections. (Paul Hennessy/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)
 With Election Day approaching, early voting begins in multiple states on Monday as the GOP and Democrats jockey for both federal and state-level political power during the midterm elections.
Early voting locations are opening today in Alaska, Arkansas, Colorado, Connecticut, South Carolina, and Texas, as well as some parts of Florida.
 Some of the widely-watched races in those states include the Florida gubernatorial contest between Rep. Byron Donalds, R-Fla., and former Rep. David Jolly, the U.S. Senate race in South Carolina where Sen. Darline Graham, the sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, is seeking a full six-year Senate term, and the U.S. Senate race in Texas, where state Attorney General Ken Paxton, a Republican, is facing Democratic state Rep. James Talarico.
 Posted by Alex Nitzberg Share US Chamber of Commerce throws support behind Paxton in widely-watched US Senate contest
Texas Republican Senate candidate, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton speaks during a rally at Southern Roots Brewing Co. on Oct. 17, 2026 in Killeen, Texas. (Joel Angel Juarez/Getty Images)
 The U.S. Chamber of Commerce has endorsed Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton for U.S. Senate.
 Paxton is facing Democratic state Rep. James Talarico in the Lone Star State's U.S. Senate contest.
“The choice is clear in Texas. Attorney General Ken Paxton has been a defender of free enterprise and the pro-growth policies that empower American businesses to thrive. He has pushed back against federal overreach, helped preserve a low-tax environment, and defended the energy sector from burdensome mandates," U.S. Chamber of Commerce Executive Vice President and Chief Policy Officer Neil Bradley stated .
 "Paxton understands that true economic prosperity relies on a fair and predictable justice system. We look forward to working together on meaningful legal reform that shields job creators from lawsuit abuse and red tape,” Bradley added.
 In a post 
 on X Paxton noted, "I am honored to have the endorsement of the @USChamber. In the Senate, I'll fight to cut taxes, roll back job-killing regulations, and get Washington bureaucrats out of the way of the men and women who drive our economy. Let's keep Texas the economic engine of America."
 The group had endorsed incumbent Sen. John Cornyn , R-Texas, prior to the GOP U.S. Senate primary in the Lone Star State, but after Cornyn and Paxton advanced to the primary runoff, Paxton emerged the victor.
 Posted by Alex Nitzberg Share Epstein-linked billionaire pours $500K into super PAC backing Kentucky Democrat
 ​ 
 A Kentucky Democrat campaigning against the influence of wealthy political donors is facing calls to disavow a $500,000 contribution from billionaire Reid Hoffman to a super PAC supporting his congressional bid, with his Republican opponent blasting the financial support as "dirty Epstein class money."
Hoffman contributed $500,000 to Kentuckians Not Corruption, an independent super PAC supporting Democratic congressional nominee Zach Dembo in Kentucky's 6th Congressional District, on Sept. 24, 2026, according to Federal Election Commission records. The contribution came as the group was spending heavily on television advertisements supporting Dembo and opposing his Republican opponent, former Kentucky state Sen. Ralph Alvarado . Advertising records filed with the Federal Communications Commission show the super PAC's weekly television advertising orders on Lexington's WLEX- TV increased more than sevenfold between mid-September and early October, climbing from $14,650 before Hoffman's contribution to $109, 990 for the week of Oct. 6.
 "This is really, it's dirty Epstein class money fueling Zach Dembo's campaign," Alvarado told Fox News Digital. "It's offensive."
 Click here to read more 
 Posted by Alec Schemmel Share Trump to stump for Sen. Roger Marshall during Kansas rally on Monday
 Sen. Roger Marshall, a Republican from Kansas, during a Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee confirmation hearing in Washington, D.C., on Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026. (Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
 President Donald Trump , who will seek to boost incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., at a rally in Park City on Monday, issued a Truth Social post about the upcoming event.
"I’m going to the Great State of Kansas today to Rally support for Roger Marshall, one of the absolutely best Senators in the U.S. Senate. His opponent is a Fake, and would be a DISASTER for Kansas, a State I won all three times, getting the highest vote in the history of Kansas - Such an honor! See you all later!!!" Trump declared in the post .
 Marshall, who has served in the upper Congressional chamber since early 2021, is facing Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton.
 Trump has been rallying throughout the country in a bid to help Republicans during midterm election season.

 Rep. James Comer, R-Ky. 
, chair of the House Oversight Committee, discusses a federal raid on the Washington, D.C. home of Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., amid financial and immigration investigations involving the congresswoman, on "Sunday Night in America."
 Posted by Eric Mack Share Europe's problems could very well be America's problems: Brian Kilmeade
 ​ 
 Fox News host Brian Kilmeade discussed the continued unrest in France on "One Nation."
 The violence from left-wing activists in Europe is a stark warning for America in the midterm elections.
 "The cost of its government promises is growing faster than its ability to pay for them," he says in his monologue.
 "It's going to snap."
 Posted by Eric Mack Share DOJ anti-hate tour launches in Michigan amid El-Sayed terror watchlist controversy
 ​ 
 Leo Terrell, from the Task Force to Combat Antisemitism, joined Fox News' "Fox & Friends First" to discuss the Department of Justice's anti-hate tour in Michigan .
 The discussion follows Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed confirming his sister-in-law's lawsuit over being placed on the federal terror watchlist.
 Posted by Eric Mack Share 
Trump takes aim at Roy Cooper over COVID-era releases amid battle for Senate seat in North Carolina
 ​ 
 President Donald Trump targeted Democratic North Carolina Sen.-nominee Roy Cooper over his record as governor, accusing him of releasing convicted murderers during the COVID-19 pandemic, pointing to the alleged August 2025 killer of Iryna Zarutska: Decarlos Brown Jr .
“Gov. Roy Cooper released this man, who then killed beautiful Iryna Zarutska,” Trump wrote late Sunday night on Truth Social. “He then released 83 other murderers, so they wouldn’t catch COVID while in jail, who went on to kill 25 people!”
 Trump’s post comes as Republicans seek to defend their narrow Senate majority in the 2026 midterm elections. Cooper, a former two-term governor, is facing a challenge from Republican Michael Whatley , the former chair of the Republican National Committee.
 Posted by Eric Mack Share Jeffries says Democrats have momentum in fight for House majority
 ​ 
 House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries says the political climate remains favorable to Democrats as the party works to retake the House majority.
 Jeffries campaigned Sunday in Ohio alongside longtime Democratic Rep. Marcy Kaptur, whose Toledo-area district is considered crucial to the fight for control of the chamber.
 Republicans are targeting Kaptur’s seat after President Donald Trump carried the district, while Kaptur is seeking another term after decades in Congress.
 Jeffries argued that Democrats are making the case for “dramatic change” and accused Republicans of being out of touch with voters concerned about affordability.
The Democratic leader also criticized Trump’s decision to waive new sanctions on Russia, saying Democrats and Republicans could pursue legislation that would limit the president’s ability to lift them.
 The Associated Press contributed to this report. 
In this photo taken with a smart phone, Rep. Marcy Kaptur, left, and House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries walk before a church services as they campaign for the midterm elections, Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, in battleground Toledo, Ohio. (AP Photo/Lisa Mascaro)
 Posted by Bradford Betz Share Latino voters who backed Trump could help decide House control
 ​ 
 Latino voters who helped return President Donald Trump to the White House in 2024 could play a decisive role in determining control of Congress this November.
 Democrats are counting on disaffected Trump supporters in heavily Latino districts across Arizona, Colorado and Texas to swing back toward the party or stay home.
 Voters interviewed in those communities cited frustration with gas prices, grocery costs and the economy. About 6 in 10 Hispanic voters disapprove of Trump’s handling of the presidency , while more than 7 in 10 disapprove of his performance on the economy, according to an October AP-NORC poll.
The potential shift does not necessarily reflect strong support for Democrats. Many Latino voters describe themselves as independent or express dissatisfaction with both parties.
JoAnna Mendoza (D), standing second from right, an Arizona Congressional District 6 candidate, talks with campaign volunteers before a weekly neighborhood canvass, Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026, in Oro Valley, Ariz. (AP Photo/Mike Christy)
